context: Evaluate levers: raise the 30s waitForDataLoaded timeout; add Playwright test-level retries for the explorer e2e job; cap/tune parallel workers so DuckDB-WASM is not starved; or reclassify the Chromium full suite as non-blocking (like WebKit/Firefox) until robust. Measure DuckDB-WASM load time under load to choose. Do not weaken real assertions to mask genuine failures.
description: During the tuning-followups batch (2026-07-23/24), PRs #1287 and #1289 each needed 3+ Chromium full-suite e2e re-runs and WebKit smoke failed on every run. Root cause: waitForDataLoaded (results-explorer/e2e/support/fixtures.ts:28) hits its 30s timeout because DuckDB-WASM data does not load in time under parallel-worker CI load. Failures SHUFFLE across unrelated specs each run (Compare, ResultDetail, responsive, index-sort-headers, external-corpus) -- resource-starvation flakiness, not a code regression. Prior items fix-chromium-result-detail-sort-flake (done) and stabilize-webkit-browser-smoke-flake-under-parallel-workers (done) did NOT hold and need superseding. Distinct from chromium-blocking-suite-not-in-required-checks (that WIRES the gate; this makes the suite reliable).

deferrals.reason: Root cause is in results-explorer/src/**, which this item lists as do_not_modify. The e2e change is mitigation only (re-navigation retries); residual flake remains at any data-bound assertion still waiting single-shot.
deferrals.summary: Fix the cold-snapshot zero-row race in results-explorer/src: gate the first keyed DuckDB-WASM query on a queryable snapshot, or re-query when it returns zero rows instead of rendering the empty state permanently

preserves.behavior: App behavior is unchanged; this is test-harness and CI robustness only
Do not weaken or delete real e2e assertions to paper over genuine failures
The blocking gate keeps its ability to catch real regressions

verifications.description: Explorer Chromium e2e passes without per-test re-runs across consecutive runs

work_units.evidence: Premise partly wrong. Reproduced locally (idle machine, --workers=1, retries=0): run 1 = 4 failed at waitForDataLoaded. But (a) the item's '30s timeout' is stale — #1307 already raised it to 45s/90s/retries2; (b) chromium has run --workers=1 since #417 (May), so #1307's 'parallel workers' diagnosis was false; (c) CI has been green 3/3 since #1307 merged 07-25
work_units.summary: Re-validate that the waitForDataLoaded flakiness still reproduces and the two prior stabilization items are done-but-ineffective

work_units.evidence: Measured: every failure burns the FULL 45s and the element never appears; perf spec reports DuckDB-WASM cold init P50=564ms/P95=978ms and data-after-init P50=6ms. So it is not latency. Real cause = cold-snapshot zero-row race (first keyed query answers 0 rows, view renders empty, never re-queries) — confirmed 3x where a shell heading rendered while rows/heatmap/grid stayed absent. Lever chosen: re-navigation between attempts (only action that clears it), NOT a bigger budget
work_units.summary: Measure DuckDB-WASM load time under parallel CI load and choose the lever

work_units.evidence: fixtures.ts: 3 attempts (20s+12s+12s=44s, preserves prior worst case) re-navigating to the entry URL between attempts; new waitForResultRows() gates on real tbody rows instead of a shell heading. Applied at the 6 sites that flaked. Stability: 3 consecutive clean local runs (111 passed, retries=0) vs baseline 2 of 4 runs failing; suite time 6.3m -> 2.4m
work_units.summary: Apply the chosen fix and demonstrate stability across consecutive runs
